observations.text:
The following deficiencies were observed in the sprinkler room:
- The new sprinkler riser has not been installed in accordance with the approved design drawings. The flow switch is required to be located a minimum of 2 ft above the check valve. Additionally, drains are required to be provided for the riser check valve and on the downstream side of the flow switch.
- A new spare sprinkler cabinet, complete with a spare sprinkler list, the required spare sprinklers, and a sprinkler wrench, has not been provided, as required per NFPA 13.
- Pipe stands are required to be constructed of minimum 2" Schedule 40 pipe. The pipe stands currently installed do not meet this requirement.
- The hydraulic placard and owner's information certificate have not been provided, as required per NFPA 13.
- Labels identifying new valves and systems have not been provided.

Level 2 in-rack sprinklers have not been installed in accordance with the approved sprinkler design drawings. Per the design drawings, Level 1 and Level 2 in-rack sprinklers are required to be staggered. The contractor shall rectify the installation accordingly.
New sprinkler piping penetrating the office interstitial space shall be sealed.
A new firestopping assembly, listed and installed in accordance with CAN/ULC-S115, is required to be provided at this location between the two tenant spaces.

In-rack sprinklers are required to be provided with arm-overs extending into the mid-bay of the rack, as indicated on the approved sprinkler design drawings. The contractor shall rectify the installation accordingly.

In-rack sprinklers shall be located a maximum of 1 inch from the rack uprights; the current installation exceeds this maximum clearance. Additionally, Level 1 in-rack sprinklers are required to be staggered relative to the Level 2 in-rack sprinklers, as required by the approved design drawings. The contractor shall rectify the installation in accordance with the design drawings.
The hose station drop shall be provided with an additional hanger located closer to the drop, in accordance with NFPA 13, Section 17.4.3.5.
The hose station drop shall be provided with an additional hanger located closer to the drop, in accordance with NFPA 13, Section 17.4.3.5.
The existing portable fire extinguisher is a 3-A rated unit. A new 6-A rated extinguisher is required to be provided at this location.

Extinguisher identification signage has been observed to be mounted too low throughout the building and is not visible along normal paths of travel, as required. Signage shall be remounted at a height of 12'-0" A.F.F. in warehouse areas and at 8'-0" A.F.F. in areas below the mezzanine.

Pallet loads are required to have a minimum of 50% clear opening free of shrink wrap to permit adequate sprinkler water penetration. The owner shall remove excess shrink wrap from pallet loads to achieve compliance.

The cage enclosures have not been provided with designated man doors for means of egress. The existing sliding doors secured with padlocks do not constitute compliant means of egress. The owner shall provide man doors in both cage enclosures to satisfy egress requirements in accordance with the Ontario Building Code.

The 'Big Ass Fan' installed at this location is classified as a High Volume Low Speed (HVLS) fan. The following requirements apply and shall be provided:
- The HVLS fan shall be centered approximately between four adjacent sprinklers.
- The vertical clearance from the HVLS fan blade to the sprinkler deflector shall be a minimum of 36 in. (900 mm).
- All HVLS fans shall be interlocked to shut down immediately upon a waterflow alarm signal via the fire alarm system, in accordance with NFPA 13.
At the time of inspection, the fan appeared to be positioned between four adjacent sprinklers; however, vertical clearance could not be confirmed during the site visit. The fan interlock with the fire alarm system for shutdown upon waterflow alarm has not been provided and is required to be installed.

The 'Big Ass Fan' installed at this location is classified as a High Volume Low Speed (HVLS) fan. The following requirements apply and shall be provided:
- The HVLS fan shall be centered approximately between four adjacent sprinklers.
- The vertical clearance from the HVLS fan blade to the sprinkler deflector shall be a minimum of 36 in. (900 mm).
- All HVLS fans shall be interlocked to shut down immediately upon a waterflow alarm signal via the fire alarm system, in accordance with NFPA 13.
At the time of inspection, the fan appeared to be positioned between four adjacent sprinklers; however, vertical clearance could not be confirmed during the site visit. The fan interlock with the fire alarm system for shutdown upon waterflow alarm has not been provided and is required to be installed.

The emergency lighting units currently installed do not appear to be high-output industrial type fixtures, as required by the approved design drawings. Additionally, the units have been mounted at an angle that prevents the remote heads from adequately illuminating the floor area. The contractor shall provide product cut sheets for the installed emergency lighting units. If the installed units are not confirmed to be high-output industrial type, the units shall be replaced with the specified type and remounted so that the remote heads provide the required floor-level illumination.
An emergency lighting unit has not been provided at this location, as required by the approved design drawings.

Donnelly Wing Sprinkler Room

Pressure regulating station appears to feed to the low pressure standpipe zone.  The current valve arrangement are incorrect and do not meet the requirements for NFPA 14, 10.2.5.  In particular, the following clauses are not met: 

(2) A method to isolate the pressure-regulating device(s) shall be provided for maintenance and repair.
(3) To provide redundancy, pressure-regulating devices shall be arranged in series so that the failure of any single device does not allow pressure in excess of 175 psi (12 bar) to any of the multiple hose connections downstream.
(4) An equally sized bypass around the pressure-regulating device(s), with a normally closed control valve, shall be installed.
(6) The pressure-regulating device shall be provided with inlet and outlet pressure gauges.
(7) The fire department connection(s) shall be connected to the system side of the outlet isolation valve.
(8) The pressure-regulating device shall be provided with a pressure relief valve in accordance with the manufacturer’s recommendations.
(9) Remote monitoring and supervision for detecting high pressure failure of the pressure-regulating device shall be provided in accordance with NFPA 72.

A figure has been provided below which provides a proper pressure regulating device arrangement.  Further hydraulic calculations will need to be completed before changes can be made.

Donnelly Wing Sprinkler Room

Existing fire pump is old and is recommended to be replaced.  The fire pump itself is not provided with any placards which would indicate its rated capacity and pressure outputs.  It would be difficult to perform testing as per OFC, 6.6.3.5. without knowledge of its designed performance outputs.  

"Fire pumps shall be tested annually at full rated capacity to ensure that they are capable of delivering the rated flow."

Donnelly Wing Sprinkler Room

Each valve in general is recommended to be labelled so that maintenance and emergency response personnel can easily identify the location they are shutting off.

B3 Sprinkler room

Pressure regulating station appears to feed to the low pressure standpipe zone.  The current valve arrangement are incorrect and do not meet the requirements for NFPA 14, 10.2.5.  In particular, the following clauses are not met: 

(2) A method to isolate the pressure-regulating device(s) shall be provided for maintenance and repair.
(3) To provide redundancy, pressure-regulating devices shall be arranged in series so that the failure of any single device does not allow pressure in excess of 175 psi (12 bar) to any of the multiple hose connections downstream.
(4) An equally sized bypass around the pressure-regulating device(s), with a normally closed control valve, shall be installed.
(6) The pressure-regulating device shall be provided with inlet and outlet pressure gauges.
(7) The fire department connection(s) shall be connected to the system side of the outlet isolation valve.
(8) The pressure-regulating device shall be provided with a pressure relief valve in accordance with the manufacturer’s recommendations.
(9) Remote monitoring and supervision for detecting high pressure failure of the pressure-regulating device shall be provided in accordance with NFPA 72.

A figure has been provided below which provides a proper pressure regulating device arrangement.  Further hydraulic calculations will need to be completed before changes can be made.

B3 Sprinkler Room

Existing sprinkler fire pump is not working.  This fire pump appears to feed majority of the sprinkler protection in the building.  Fixing this fire pump should be considered high priority and should be fixed / replaced as soon as possible.  

Fire pump replacements is not a simple like-for-like swap as the fire protection engineer needs to accept liability that the fire pump is adequately sized for the systems it serves.  Thus, hydraulic calculations of the most remote systems which the pump serves is required.

B2-038

Queen MRI Bypass water supply is current shut off.  This line appears to be the second water in-coming into this sprinkler room header.   2012 Ontario Building Code, 3.2.9.7.(4) required this building to be served by two sources of water supply from the public water system.  This valve should be re-opened to meet this requirement.

B2-038

A line leads to the CCN: B2 Shutter Water Tie In #136.  The valve is opened however, it presently does not appear to lead anywhere.  It is also noted that Shutter sprinkler room is recently demolished.  

If the line is not currently feeding any systems, the valve should be closed and marked accordingly.  There is potential this line is the second incoming to the new room.  The engineering team for the Shutter building modifications should be reached out to confirm current status.

B2-038 

Existing B2-038 Main Wet Below Grade system valve currently has a flow switch programmed as a low-pressure signal.  Flow switch shall be re-programmed as an alarm signal.

Basement Main Electrical Room

There are small rooms on either side of the main electrical gearbox.  These rooms contain dry-wall ceilings with no sprinkler protection provided in the rooms.  The rooms are required to be provided with sprinkler protection.  There are two methods to resolve this issue:
1. If the rooms are categorised as a fire separation with 1 hour fire resistance rating, drops with equivalent pipe diameter to the branchlines at the above ceiling can be provided to feed the sprinklers.  The architect who designed the room will need to provide this information.  At present however, there are upgrades required until it can be considered a fire separation, including providing a rated door from the room into the electrical room, and providing fire stopping assembly on the room penetrations.  
2. Remove the dropped ceiling so that the overhead ceiling sprinkler protection can protect the space.
3. Perform hydraulic calculations and provide new sprinklers into the rooms accordingly.

PGT Sprinkler Room

Current fire pump and jockey pump sensing line configurations do not have test connections c/w tee, valve, second tee, and second valve on both near the fire pump and near the fire pump controller as per NFPA 20, 4.32.5 and A.4.32(a).

PGT Sprinkler Room

The fire pump and PRV gauges provided do not appear to be liquid filled gauges.  NFPA 20 recommends liquid filled gauges be used for more accurate pressure readings.

Bond Wing Rooftop Penthouse

There are a high amount of obstructions here due to the overhead ceiling sprinkler protection due to HVAC and ductwork.  NFPA 13, 2025, 10.2.8.2 requires obstructions aggregate over 4ft in width shall be provided with sprinkler protection underneath.  At present, there are two locations which appears additional sprinklers are required.  See pictures for the areas.

61 Queen Street Basement Sprinkler Room

Existing sprinkler systems contains a water motor gong.  It is highly difficult to trace the line for the gong and its strainers.  The sprinkler systems are provided with existing flow switch devices to detect a system alarm.  The water motor gong is thus redundant as NFPA 13, 16.11.1 is an or statement to provide alarm, horn, or siren.  The waterflow alarm to the fire alarm system shall be confirmed that the correct annunciation is provided.  The water motor gong can be removed provided confirmation.

209 Victoria Street Mechanical Penthouse 

The existing glycol system feeding into the generator room contains a flow switch on the glycol side of the system.  The present configuration would make it impossible to test the flow switch without discharging glycol.  There are two potential options to rectify this item:
1. Relocate existing vane type flow switch between the system control valve and check valve.  Note that there is potential for false flow switch activation due to water hammer as the check valve located downstream of the flow switch will not allow it to dampen the water movement.  
2. Replace existing Glycol system with a dry-pipe system.

209 Victoria Street Mechanical Penthouse 

The existing glycol system incoming main is not provided with a 1" axillary drain as required by NFPA 13, 16.10.5.2.1.  This should be provided for adequate draining purposes.
